lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

To protect Arrive AI’s intellectual property, Arrive relies on a combination of laws and regulations, as well as contractual restrictions.

Our future capital requirements will depend on many factors, including:

Our future success will depend upon our ability to keep pace with technological developments and to timely address the increasingly sophisticated needs of our customers by supporting existing and new technologies and by developing and introducing enhancements to our current products and new products in our future commercial operations.
In addition, we may experience difficulties internally or in conjunction with key vendors and partners that could delay or prevent successful development, introduction and sale of our products.
The expansion of these markets in general, and the market for our products and services in particular, depends on a number of factors, including the following:
Our future growth depends on our gaining market acceptance and regular production orders for our products and services.
Our business depends on intellectual property licensed from our Chief Executive Officer.
We rely on patents licensed pursuant to our Exclusive Patent License Agreement.

If we are unable to anticipate or adapt to such advancements, or if we fail to allocate our resources efficiently, we may be forced to rely on outdated equipment that becomes increasingly inefficient and expensive to maintain.
Our Mailbox-as-a-Service model depends on customer adoption, subscription renewals, and predictable recurring revenue.
We rely on third-party cloud providers, and disruptions or pricing changes by such providers could adversely impact operations.
Our platform depends on our users’ internet access.
Furthermore, as the rate of adoption of new technologies increases, the networks our platform relies on may not be able to sufficiently adapt to any increased demand for our products.
We also rely on third-party providers, including cloud storage and infrastructure providers, whose security practices we do not directly control.
Our ability to continue as a going concern depends on our ability to generate sufficient cash flows from operations, obtain additional financing, or some combination thereof.

Our ability to obtain additional financing will depend on a number of factors, including general market conditions, investor acceptance of our business model, our financial condition and results of operations, and conditions in the debt and equity markets.
While we rely on our MSP for day-to-day IT operations and security management functions, responsibility for oversight of cybersecurity risk remains with our management and Board of Directors.
We rely on patented and non-patented proprietary information relating to product development, manufacturing capabilities, and other core competencies of our business.
Our potential for growth depends on continued permission and acceptance by local governments and municipalities of autonomous robot and drone deliveries.

Our future capital expenditures will depend on many factors, including, but not limited to our growth, our ability to attract and retain customers, market acceptance of our offerings, the time and extent of spending to support our efforts to develop our platform, the expansion of sales and marketing activities, and the timing and extent of spending for initiatives.
